facts.fact: Leah 回家已三周，叙述者（Miri）基本已习惯这一切
facts.anchor: She’s been home three weeks and I’m mostly used to everything.

facts.fact: Miri 以替非营利组织写资助申请为生，一直在家工作
facts.anchor: I write grant applications for non-profit organisations for a living

facts.fact: Leah 突然说受不了楼上电视的噪音
facts.anchor: “I can’t stand this,” Leah says suddenly.

facts.fact: Miri 上楼去敲邻居的门，但没人应门
facts.anchor: I go upstairs and hammer on the door but the neighbours don’t answer

facts.fact: Miri 意识到自己从未真正见过邻居，一切只是间接证据
facts.anchor: I have never actually laid eyes on the neighbours

facts.fact: Miri 六分钟后回来，发现 Leah 已从客厅角落移进浴室并开着两个水龙头
facts.anchor: Leah has moved from the corner of the living room and is locked in the bathroom, running both the taps.

facts.fact: Leah 把中心寄来的助眠电箱带进浴室并打开
facts.anchor: She has, it appears, taken the electric box she uses to sleep into the bathroom

facts.fact: Miri 记得 Leah 本应离开三周却失踪了六个月，无人知道发生了什么
facts.anchor: gone for three weeks and disappeared for six months

relations.kind: 多年伴侣，彼此已融为一体、难分难解
relations.anchor: a point before Leah and I became this fused, inextricable thing

relations.kind: 她过去常深夜上楼请他们把电视关小
relations.anchor: Leah used to go up there sometimes, knock on the door late at night and ask them to turn it down.

relations.kind: 同住多年却从未见过面，只凭脚步声与音乐推断其存在
relations.anchor: I have never actually laid eyes on the neighbours

relations.kind: 中心寄来助眠电箱、减压袜与格言书作为离别赠礼
relations.anchor: a parting gift from the Centre
